title: SourceReadle Puzzle
description: One daily puzzle: a code snippet with exactly one vulnerability, solved in three stages (find the line, name the bug class, pick the correct fix).

scaffold.description: Heavy-scaffolding mode (used by the Intro tier): the player pre-highlights the vulnerable line, gives unlimited taps, shows only two options per choice stage, and keeps hints visible. Guides a beginner to near-certain success.

snippet.description: The code the player reads. One or more files; lines are 1-indexed per file.

code.description: Verbatim source, newline-separated. Rendered with 1-indexed line numbers.

notes.description: Explain-mode annotations: map of 1-indexed line number (as a string) to a plain-English description of what that line does. Sparse is fine — annotate the non-obvious lines. Neutral descriptions; do not give away which line is the vulnerability.

line.description: Stage 1: locate the vulnerable line. Guesses are (file, line). Feedback is green/yellow/grey.

file.description: Name of the file in snippet.files that holds the bug.

yellowRadius.description: A guess within this many lines of the answer (same file) is yellow.

bugClass.description: Stage 2: name the vulnerability class. Options drawn from the shared taxonomy. Yellow = right family, wrong specific class.

answer.description: Must be one of options and a key in taxonomy.json.

why.description: Stage 3 (training): understand the mechanism. Pick the explanation of WHY the line is exploitable. Exactly one correct.

prompt.description: Optional override for the question text.

label.description: A candidate explanation of the mechanism.

whyWrong.description: Shown after answering, for incorrect options. Omit on the correct one.

fix.description: Stage 4: pick the patch that actually closes the hole. Exactly one correct.

diff.description: Unified-diff-style snippet of the proposed fix.

whyWrong.description: Shown after solving for the incorrect options. Omit on the correct one.

source.description: Provenance. Required for every puzzle so attribution and licensing travel with it.

origin.description: 'original' = written by us; 'cve' = derived from a real advisory.

fixCommit.description: URL of the upstream fix commit.

license.description: SPDX id of the source project's license, e.g. 'GPL-2.0-only'.

training.description: Teaching material. 'exploit' and 'concepts' enrich the result screen; 'hints' power Learn mode.

exploit.description: Markdown: a concrete malicious input and what it yields. Explanatory, not a weaponized tool.

concepts.description: Tags such as 'CWE-89', 'OWASP A03:2021' for filtering and linking.

hints.description: One short hint per stage, revealed on demand in Learn mode.

writeup.description: Released the day AFTER the puzzle. Explains why the line is dangerous and points at real code to read next.

summary.description: Markdown. Why it's exploitable and how the fix closes it.

verify.description: Optional execution contract (Phase 1). Lets a sandboxed runner prove the answer key by running a PoC against the original snippet and against every fix option. Convention: the PoC process EXIT CODE is the oracle — exit 0 means the vulnerability was successfully exploited; any non-zero exit (assertion, error, crash, timeout) counts as blocked.

image.description: Container image the runner uses, e.g. 'python:3.12-slim' or 'gcc:13'.

build.description: Shell commands run in the work dir before 'run' (compiling, etc.). Absent/empty for interpreted languages.

run.description: Shell command that runs the PoC. Exit 0 == exploited; any non-zero == blocked.

network.description: Whether the sandbox allows network. Keep false unless the PoC genuinely needs loopback.

harness.description: Extra files written alongside the snippet to make it runnable (a PoC driver, a build file). Not shown to the player.

original.description: The baseline program = snippet.files + harness, with no fix applied. Must be exploitable.

fixes.description: Index-aligned with stages.fix.options. For each option the runner overlays 'files' onto the baseline snippet (matched by file name), then runs the PoC. Exactly the correct fix (stages.fix.answerIndex) must expect 'blocked'; every other option must expect 'exploited'.

files.description: Complete content of each file this fix changes relative to the baseline snippet (by name). Files not listed are taken from snippet.files unchanged.
